newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 7.

text.p: The focus of Waitangi Day commemorations will shift back to Waitangi this year, with National set to backtrack under the influence of coalition partner NZ First. Senior National ministers, including deputy leader Don McKinnon, are now expected to attend the ceremony, despite National saying before the election it would not go to Waitangi. Official Waitangi Day commemorations were moved to Government House in Wellington last year after abuse of dignitaries -- including spitting at governor-general Dame Catherine Tizard -- at Waitangi in 1995.

The Treaty of Waitangi should tour New Zealand to celebrate the year 2000, Internal Affairs Minister Jack Elder has suggested. However, the extremely fragile condition of the historic documents could mean Elder's plan is unworkable. Elder said the treaty, which is displayed at the National Archives in Wellington, was the founding document of New Zealand and everyone should have a chance to see it. Page 2.

Health Minister Bill English moved on Monday to reassure the public the government intended to deliver on its health policy, after fallout from his earlier acknowledgment that some costings were "purely theoretical". "The government is committed to progress in all areas outlined in the coalition document," he said on Monday. Page 2.

The Conservation Department has told police it is to withdraw from helping with search and rescue activities at Mt Cook from the end of summer, after announcing it was no longer prepared to recover bodies. It has told police they must establish their own system for recovering bodies, because it uses too much of the department's resources. The announcement follows the death of a German tourist on the Tasman Glacier on Saturday. His body was not recovered for 17 hours because of the department's refusal to retrieve bodies. Page 3.

The Manufacturers Federation on Monday urged Treasurer Winston Peters to "deliver on his promises to bring the dollar down" by cutting government expenditure. The dollar was on Monday nudging US71 cents, and the trade-weighted index of leading currencies topped 68. Manfed chief executive Simon Arnold said the government's short-term lever for bringing down the currency was cutting spending. "We're suggesting that if they can cut anything out using the razor gang that they should stick it in the bank rather than spend up on further policies," he said. Page 13.

Job losses at Comalco's Tiwai Point smelter would follow a review of operations, the company said on Monday. General manager David Brewer said the review would initially look at support and services roles, while a separate review would examine metal-making processes. He said there would be some reduction in the number of support and service roles, but it was not expected there would be much impact on people in operational and production areas. Brewer said he hoped reductions would be achieved through "voluntary means". Page 13.

Lend Lease Corp said on Monday it was holding preliminary discussions on the acquisition of United States property group Equity Real Estate Investment Management. "No binding agreement has been reached, and any such agreement would be subject to approval by regulatory authorities," Lend Lease said. Equitable Real Estate (ERE) is the largest United States manager of real estate equity and mortgage investments, with about US$25 billion (NZ$35 billion) of funds under management. Page 13.
